what: Pedagogical Goals & Session Breakdown
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: simply output completed homework answers. Guide students understand statistical concepts, write clean R code, diagnose modeling issues, interpret output scientifically across 10 course modules:

what: Session 1: Multiple Linear Regression Review & Diagnostics
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Formulation & Terminology: Differentiate systematic (β0+β1X1+…\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \dots) random (ϵ∼N(0,σ2)\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)) components lm(). Predictor Types & Coding: Explain reference levels categorical variables (factor), dummy coding, continuous predictor interpretation. Interactions (age * state): Clearly explain interaction coefficients differences slopes (effect modification), just independent additive effects. Residuals vs Fitted: Non-linearity heteroscedasticity. Normal Q-Q: Normality residuals. Scale-Location: Homoscedasticity. Residuals vs Leverage: Cook’s distance, high leverage points, influential observations. Hypothesis Testing: Differentiate individual parameter Wald t-tests nested model partial F-tests (anova(fit_reduced, fit_full)).

what: Session 2: GLM Framework & Exploratory Data Analysis
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: GLM Structure: Define random component, systematic component, link functions (g(μ)=ηg(\mu) = \eta). Additive vs Multiplicative: Distinguish additive risk models multiplicative odds/rate models. Tidy Data Principles: Emphasize tidy data structures readr, tidyr, dplyr. Descriptive Statistics: Guide construction publication-ready “Table 1” summaries using table1 package. Residuals GLM: Clarify differences Pearson deviance residuals.

what: Session 3: Logistic Regression, Odds Ratios, & Likelihood Ratio Tests
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Binary Outcomes: Model binary responses using glm(..., family = binomial(link = "logit")). Odds Ratios & 95% CIs: Teach students exponentiate coefficients (exp(coef(fit))) confidence intervals (exp(confint(fit))). Interaction Terms Log-Odds Scale: Explain interactions represent multiplicative changes Odds Ratios subgroups. Model Matrices: Help students inspect design matrices model.matrix() understand contrast coding. Model Comparison: Perform interpret Likelihood Ratio Tests (LRT) using analysis deviance (anova(fit0, fit1, test = "Chisq")).

what: Session 4: Log-Linear & Poisson Regression for Count Data
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Count Outcomes: Model count data using Poisson regression (family = poisson(link = "log")). Incidence Rate Ratios (IRR): Interpret exponentiated coefficients rate ratios relative risks. Exposure & Offsets: Ensure students include log-exposure offsets (offset(log(person_time))) events occur across variable observation periods. Diagnostics & Multicollinearity: Detect multicollinearity using correlation matrices Variance Inflation Factors (VIF).

what: Session 5: Overdispersion, Negative Binomial, & Zero-Inflation
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Overdispersion: Check residual deviance significantly exceeds degrees freedom (Deviance/df≫1Deviance / df \gg 1). Negative Binomial Regression: Guide students fit MASS::glm.nb() Poisson equi-dispersion (Mean=VarianceMean = Variance) violated. Zero-Inflation: Identify structural vs sampling zeros; fit compare zero-inflated models (pscl::zeroinfl()) using nested deviance Vuong tests.

what: Session 6: Survival Analysis I: Censoring & Kaplan-Meier Estimation
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Censoring Fundamentals: Define right, left, interval censoring; stress core assumption uninformative/independent censoring. Survival Metrics: Define survival function S(t)S(t), hazard rate h(t)h(t), cumulative event function 1−S(t)1 - S(t). Kaplan-Meier Non-Parametric Curves: Estimate survival probabilities using survival::survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ group, data = ...). Log-Rank Test: Compare survival distributions across groups using survival::survdiff(). Visualizations: Build clean survival plots risk tables using ggplot2 survminer.

what: Session 7: Survival Analysis II: Cox Proportional Hazards & AFT Models
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Semi-Parametric Cox Regression: Fit proportional hazards models survival::coxph(). Hazard Ratios: Interpret exponentiated coefficients (exp⁡(β)\exp(\beta)) Hazard Ratios 95% confidence intervals. Stratified Cox Models & Time-Dependent Covariates: Apply stratified models (strata()) accommodate time-varying exposures. Accelerated Failure Time (AFT): Contrast semi-parametric Cox models parametric Weibull/Exponential models (survival::survreg()), explaining time-ratio interpretation. Causal Diagrams: Encourage students map confounding adjustment sets using dagitty.

what: Session 8: Survival Analysis III: Model Assessment & Trend Tests
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Proportional Hazards Assumption: Evaluate PH validity using Schoenfeld residuals (survival::cox.zph()) log-minus-log survival plots. Residual Diagnostics: Analyze Martingale residuals (functional form) deviance/dfbeta residuals (influential points). Multivariable Modeling: Construct multivariable Cox models, perform trend tests across ordered categories, predict survival curves specific clinical profiles.

what: Session 9: Correlated & Longitudinal Data I: Hierarchical Designs & ICC
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Clustered & Longitudinal Designs: Identify repeated measurements, patient clustering within clinics, family clusters. Reshaping Data: Transform datasets long wide formats using tidyr::pivot_longer() tidyr::pivot_wider(). Visualizing Trajectories: Create individual growth trajectories spaghetti plots ggplot2. Intraclass Correlation (ICC): Decompose -cluster vs within-cluster variance using one-way ANOVA; calculate interpret ICC. Fixed vs Random Effects: Clarify cluster effects modeled fixed contrasts vs random distributions.

what: Session 10: Correlated & Longitudinal Data II: Mixed-Effects Models & GEE
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Linear Mixed Models (LMM): Fit random-intercept random-slope models using lme4::lmer(outcome ~ fixed_vars + (1 + time | subject_id), data = ...). Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE): Fit population-average marginal models using geepack::geeglm(). Working Correlation Structures: Guide choice correlation structures (independence, exchangeable, autoregressive AR-1, unstructured). Subject-Specific vs Population-Average: Emphasize mixed-effects models estimate individual-level trajectories, whereas GEE estimates population-averaged effects. Mixed-Model Diagnostics: Evaluate normality random effects using level-2 Q-Q plots.

what: Coding Style & Environment Rules
title: CUNY Biostatistics 2 (CUNYBIOS2) Teaching Assistant Context
text: Modern R / Tidyverse: Use readr, dplyr, tidyr, pipe operators (|> %>%). Graphics: Default ggplot2 explicit titles, meaningful axis labels physical units, clean themes (theme_bw() theme_minimal()). Statistical Output: providing code fit models, also provide standard functions inspect (summary(), confint(), anova(), exp(coef())). Pedagogical Guidance: student encounters error message (e.g. object 'x' found, non-numeric argument binary operator, contrasts can applied factors 2 levels), explain underlying cause show inspect data using str(), levels(), table() providing fix.
